knowledge:
- key_parameters: E=Exposure vector or n x 1 matrix ;; M=Mediator matrix of size n x K, where K is the number of mediators ;; Y=Outcome vector or n x 1 matrix ;; Z=Optional numerical matrix of covariates (size n x number of covariates) to regress out before mediation analysis ;; nperm=Number of permutations used to estimate the null distribution (default is 100) ;; w=Optional vector of weights of length n (e.g., for case-control studies to adjust for prevalence), standardized to sum to 1 ;; useWeightsZ=Logical; if TRUE, weights in w are used in the initial regression on Z, otherwise equal weights are used
- alternatives: Standard Bonferroni correction, over which MultiMed significantly improves statistical power
- when_to_use: When testing multiple potential biological mediators (e.g., genomics, metabolomics) simultaneously between an exposure and an outcome, especially in case-control designs or when adjusting for covariates
- pitfalls: Forgetting to set a seed (set.seed) before running medTest since it relies on permutations, which can lead to non-reproducible p-values ;; Incorrectly specifying weights w or useWeightsZ in case-control studies, which can bias the exposure-mediator association ;; Inputting Z as a non-numerical matrix or data frame (it must be a numerical matrix)

workflows.name: multiple_mediation_analysis
workflows.intent: Test multiple potential mediators simultaneously between an exposure and an outcome, adjusting for covariates and applying observational weights.
input: NavyAdenoma (a data frame containing exposure, mediators, outcome, and covariates)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the MultiMed package and the dataset ;; 2. Calculate observational weights based on disease prevalence and case-control proportions ;; 3. Run the mediation test using medTest with specified permutations, covariates, and weights ;; 4. Identify the top mediators by sorting or filtering the resulting p-values
workflows.code:
library(MultiMed)
data(NavyAdenoma)
prev <- 0.228
p <- sum(NavyAdenoma$Adenoma==1)/nrow(NavyAdenoma)
w <- rep(NA, nrow(NavyAdenoma))
w[NavyAdenoma$Adenoma == 1] <- prev/p
w[NavyAdenoma$Adenoma == 0] <- (1-prev)/(1-p)
set.seed(840218)
medsFish <- medTest(E=NavyAdenoma$Fish,
                    M=NavyAdenoma[, 6:154],
                    Y=NavyAdenoma$Adenoma,
                    Z=NavyAdenoma[, 2:5],
                    nperm=1000, w=w,
                    useWeightsZ=FALSE)
rownames(medsFish) <- colnames(NavyAdenoma[,-c(1:5, 154)])
medsFish[which.min(medsFish[,"p"]),,drop=FALSE]
